content.title: HTML to PDF and images in pure Go
content.lede: gowkhtmltopdf exposes the internal convert and imageout pipelines through an idiomatic pure-Go surface: build a Converter or ImageConverter, set wkhtmltopdf-style dotted settings, attach callbacks, and Convert. The module import path is gowkhtmltopdf.

content.heading: PDF converter in Go

sections.heading: Dotted names and defaults
sections.body: Both GlobalSettings.Set and ObjectSettings.Set take wkhtmltopdf-style dotted keys: size.pagesize, orientation, margin.top, header.left, footer.right, load.* and web.*. Unknown names return an error, and Get reads a key back in canonical string form. NewGlobalSettings and NewObjectSettings start from the upstream wkhtmltopdf defaults (A4 portrait, 10 mm margins, background on), mirroring upstream where implemented. The same examples/pdf example drives these calls from CLI-style flags, including the identical local file ACL pair.
bullets: Global keys: size.pagesize, margin.top, orientation, title, pdfversion, pdfprofile, outline, enablelocalfileaccess, and the web.* / load.* families.
Object keys: page, web.images, header.left, footer.right, load.jsdelay, load.blocklocalfileaccess, and friends.
web.images=false set globally disables fetch and paint in both PDF and image mode.

sections.heading: The local file ACL pair
sections.body: Both halves are required before a normal local path converts: global enablelocalfileaccess=true and object load.blocklocalfileaccess=false. This matches the CLI pair of --enable-local-file-access with the blocked-by-default load policy. AddObject copies the object's settings, so later mutations of s do not affect the converter.
bullets: SetPage accepts a path, a URL, or an inline:/data: source.
SetBody(html, base) treats the bytes as an in-memory document with base resolving relative subresources, and AddHTML chains the same into a converter.
ConvertHTML(ctx, html, global) is a one-shot helper that returns PDF bytes without creating a temp input file; linked local assets still need the ACL pair.

sections.heading: Typed builders
sections.body: For compile-time-checked configuration, NewPdfGlobalOptions returns a typed builder with WithPageSize, WithPDFVersion, WithPDFProfile, WithMargins, WithTitle, WithCopies, WithOutline, WithSmartShrinking, WithBackground, WithCompression and WithResolveRelativeLinks; Build() yields GlobalSettings. PDFRequest plus RunPDF is the type-safe one-shot API, writing output to an io.Writer instead of returning bytes. WithPDFVersion / WithPDFProfile shipped in 0.2.2. WithPDFVersion accepts "1.4" (default), "1.7", or "2.0" and stores the canonical token on pdfversion; version alone is not a PDF/A or PDF/UA claim. WithPDFProfile accepts aliases such as a3a-ua1 / a3a / ua1 (PDF 1.7) and a4-ua2 / a4 / ua2 (PDF 2.0), or the canonical names, and stores the canonical token on pdfprofile. After WithPDFProfile("a3a-ua1"), Get("pdfprofile") is "PDF/A-3a+PDF/UA-1".

content.heading: PDF version and profile
content.code:
opts := gowkhtmltopdf.NewPdfGlobalOptions().
	WithPDFVersion("1.7").    // optional: "1.4" (default), "1.7", or "2.0"
	WithPDFProfile("a3a-ua1") // aliases a3a, ua1, a4-ua2, a4, ua2 also work
global := opts.Build()
name, _ := global.Get("pdfprofile") // "PDF/A-3a+PDF/UA-1", not "a3a-ua1"

// Dotted keys are equivalent:
_ = global.Set("pdfversion", "2.0")
_ = global.Set("pdfprofile", "a4-ua2")

content.heading: Image converter in Go
Key types and the synchronous model
rows: PDF pipeline; config via Global() and AddObject, then Convert(ctx).
Convert runs synchronously and replaces Output(); a converter needs at least one object, else ErrNoPageObjectsAdded. Output returns a copy of the PDF bytes.
wkhtmltoimage counterpart; renders the first added page.
Default 1024 px smart-width viewport, PNG output; Set/AddObject/Object/Convert/Output. Converting without a page returns ErrNoInputPageAdded.
Dotted-string settings surfaces with Get and Set.
Unknown names error; defaults mirror upstream wkhtmltopdf. PdfGlobalOptions offers a typed builder alternative.
Log-line callbacks on both converter types.
Severity is decided by line markers (warning:/warn:, error:/err:); errors also surface through OnError when a Convert fails.
Phase names like Loading pages (1/1), Printing pages (1/1) and Done; OnProgress receives the 0-100 percentage.
ConvertHTML returns []byte; the Run* functions write to req.Output and cannot carry image-mode settings in a PDF request, giving compile-time safety.

content.title: Module path and install
content.body: go.mod declares the module path github.com/chinmay-sawant/gowkhtmltopdf plus two allowlisted direct pure-Go modules: github.com/go-text/typesetting for OpenType shaping and github.com/tdewolff/canvas for SVG rasterization. Their transitive graph is resolved by Go; no cgo, browser, or native converter process is required. LibraryVersion tracks the upstream 0.12.x compatibility surface as 0.12.7-dev, while VERSION is the project's release number (currently 0.2.3). Install the library with go get github.com/chinmay-sawant/gowkhtmltopdf@v0.2.3, or point a checkout with go mod edit -replace github.com/chinmay-sawant/gowkhtmltopdf=/path/to/gowkhtmltopdf.

content.title: Planned: Python bindings
content.body: A Python package wrapping the Go library is on the roadmap and not yet released. No pip package or pythonic API exists today; until it ships, Python callers drive the gowkhtmltopdf binary as a subprocess, the same way pdfkit drives wkhtmltopdf.
